newsitem.title: UK: UK's CBI says tax cuts should not exceed one bln.
newsitem.headline: UK's CBI says tax cuts should not exceed one bln.

text.p: UK employers group the Confederation of British Industry (CBI) called today for a prudent budget by the government in November to ensure that public borrowing is moved onto a sustainable long-term path.
The CBI also called for a 2.0 billion pound trimming of the Government's spending target and said the scope for tax cuts was 1.0 billion stg.
The CBI said any relaxation of personal taxation should be directed towards higher personal allowances to take more people out of tax completely, rather than through a lower basic rate of income tax.
"This will help address the disincentive effect presently created by the combined impact of tax and benefit withdrawal," the employers group said.
"The Chancellor should have prudence as a watchword," said Andrew Buxton, chairman of the banking group Barclays and of the CBI's economic committee.

"Radical action is not needed to support competitiveness and economic growth -- what is needed above all is continuity of the more stable economic conditions we have achieved over the past four years."
The CBI said it did not want to see any cuts in education and training, nor in infrastructure spending.
-- a set of measures to help small and medium-sized businesses
-- new measures to get the unemployed back to work
-- a freeze on duties on alcohol and tobacco.
